st: Mental health: books, Netflix and finance?

sec.p: Let's face it, school curricula are more and more a thing of the past: years memorising names, dates and poems that we now pull up with Google and AI. As if that weren't enough, students keep getting worse at maths and reading, AI keeps getting better.
Breaking the theatrical “fourth wall” several times, director Jonah Hill brought his sessions with psychotherapist Phil Stutz to Netflix.
Anyway, even if we take it philosophically (Heraclitus-style), we don't like change. Around us, though, it's happening more and more often:
How can we accept change? With a book by Brad Stulberg (whom we met in 🎁 ff.68.4) maybe? After all, reading can be psychotherapy too.
A concrete example. Two of my values are sport and financial independence. They guide my everyday choices. When I do things that feed these values, I feel good.

rel: ff.117 We live in a simulation
